items.title: 襄阳大战
items.subtitle: XIANGYANG
items.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create ONE exquisite standalone vintage watercolor wuxia landscape poster, portrait 4:5, an illustrated collector's edition inspired by Jin Yong's novels. This belongs to a coherent eight-print collection.
Style: warm ivory aged paper, subtle paper fibers, fine expressive pen lines beneath transparent watercolor, layered mineral greens and dusty blue, warm ochre with restrained vermilion accents. Sophisticated atmospheric perspective, intricate but credible period architecture and tiny expressive figures. A single continuous grand landscape with foreground, middle distance and distant mountains or horizon; no panels. Let the environment occupy about 85 percent of the artwork. Human scale should convey epic vastness. Hand-painted illustration, rich detail yet breathing room. Soft faded paper margins, delicate thin corner ornament.
Typography: reserve a small clear header area, small Chinese novel name above a larger elegant dark-brown Chinese calligraphic scene title, and a tiny widely spaced English subtitle. Render the specified Chinese text accurately. No other labels or prose.
All people wear plausible Song-period Chinese or early Mongol/Central Asian clothing as appropriate. Fictional literary visualization, not a historical documentary or adaptation screenshot. No modern objects, no firearms, no luminous energy beams, no flying dragons, no photorealism, no 3D plinth, no comic panels, no watermark.

Novel header (exact): "神雕侠侣". Main title (exact): "襄阳大战". English subtitle (exact): "XIANGYANG".
Scene: A sweeping oblique panorama of besieged medieval Xiangyang: layered grey-brick ramparts and gate towers stretch across the middle, the Han River and mountains recede into smoky golden distance, immense orderly Mongol cavalry formations, standards, wooden siege engines and dust fill the field. Yang Guo, a small but readable dark-robed one-armed hero with his RIGHT arm missing and LEFT arm extended in a powerful stone-throwing gesture, occupies the near ridge overlooking the battle; a tiny projectile travels toward a distant mounted Mongol commander under command banners. Capture the novel's climactic moment without gore, not an enormous boulder. Warriors and horses are coherent groups, not visual noise. Late afternoon bronze light, immense heroic scale.

Yang Guo is a relatively small but readable single figure braced in the surf, dark rough robe, RIGHT arm missing, holding a simple unornamented WOODEN practice sword in his LEFT hand against an oncoming wave. On the main terrace a small dynamic focal pair: dark-robed Yang Guo with RIGHT arm absent and a dark heavy sword in his LEFT hand; white-robed Xiaolongnu holding slender swords. Scene: The legendary FIRST Mount Hua gathering, a conceptual tableau of the five great martial masters, NOT a tournament arena: towering sheer granite peaks, narrow snow-dusted stone ledges, a sea of cloud, twisted pines, immense distant ridges. Exactly FIVE small separated masters on a broad connected summit platform: a composed Daoist in dark simple robes (Wang Chongyang), a lean green-robed flute bearer (Huang Yaoshi), a white-robed western martial master with a staff (Ouyang Feng), a dignified southern ruler in restrained regal robes (Duan Zhixing, BEFORE becoming a monk), and a patched-robed beggar holding a bamboo staff (Hong Qigong). They regard one another, no need for synchronized attacks. No Guo Jing here. Sunrise above clouds, serene, lofty, monumental.

Scene: A poetic sweeping coastal panorama of fictional Peach Blossom Island: dense pink peach blossom groves on rugged green hills, winding paths and a modest Song-style pavilion, black shoreline rocks, translucent jade coves and an endless hazy blue sea. Huang Yaoshi, a small slender older man in plain green robes, stands on an elevated seaside rock playing a jade flute, facing the ocean. Lyrical sea mist and early spring sunlight, layered geographic scale, delicate pink against mineral green and blue.
